_comment: Published token prices, USD per 1,000,000 tokens. Data, not code, so a price change is a
data edit and shows up in a diff.
Every entry carries where the number came from and when it was read. Bedrock prices are
region-specific: these are us-east-1, which is the region the benchmark runs in. us-west-1
is materially more expensive for Nova 2 Lite ($0.39 / $3.21), so a rerun in another region

us.amazon.nova-lite-v1:0.confidence: third-party; cross-checked against the stated 5.0x ratio to Nova 2 Lite on https://aws-bedrock-explorer.com/models/amazon/nova-2-lite-v1-0

us.amazon.nova-micro-v1:0.confidence: third-party; cross-checked against the stated 8.6x ratio to Nova 2 Lite (0.30/8.6 = 0.0349)

us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0.confidence: third-party, two independent sources agree (OpenRouter and aws-bedrock-explorer.com, us-east-1 baseline)

global.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0.confidence: assumed equal to the us. profile; the global profile's price was not separately published and this is flagged as an assumption in docs/model-benchmark.md

meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct.confidence: the build.nvidia.com developer endpoint is credit-metered rather than billed per token, so a dollar cost per task is not meaningful for this candidate; recorded as zero and called out explicitly in the findings rather than silently making NVIDIA look free

nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1.5.confidence: same credit-metered endpoint as meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct above, so the same zero and the same caveat. Session G's judge. Because a zero price makes a USD ceiling blind rather than generous, evals/run.py enforces a second ceiling counted in calls rather than dollars — see docs/spike-findings.md 7.7
